summary: Camera-capacity estimator answers 'how many cameras can this host process?' New GET /api/capacity (services.EstimateCameraCapacity) models the workload across AI inference (CPU/GPU), memory, and live-view decode, reporting an estimated max with the limiting resource and per-workload breakdown. The AI figure uses three confidence tiers: a static spec-sheet model, a LIVE extrapolation from real host CPU load + active camera count once cameras are running, and a CALIBRATED figure from POST /api/capacity/calibrate, which benchmarks the actual YOLO detector (times real inferences on a synthetic frame) for an accurate cold-start estimate before any camera exists. Recording is treated as a rolling buffer: instead of capping the camera count, the disk constrains the achievable retention (ConfiguredRetentionDays / AchievableRetentionDays / RetentionConstrained). A capacity card in Settings -> Machine Health shows the estimate, Run calibration, and the retention note. The first-run wizard reuses the calibrate endpoint.
compatibility: Additive. Read-only estimate endpoint (GET, all authenticated users); calibrate is an admin POST that runs a short detector benchmark (best run while idle). All tunables are conservative, clearly-labelled assumptions (rough +/-50%) that sharpen as live load / calibration become available.
